title: isa
summary: Test class/category membership in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Returns host logical scalars and inspects resident metadata without launching kernels. Explicit gpuArray values expose wrapper identity; internal automatic residency exposes underlying host class/category semantics.

description: `isa(x, T)` returns true when value `x` belongs to class or abstract category `T`. Supported class/category checks and type coercions follow MATLAB semantics.
behaviors: Exact class names (such as `"double"`, `"cell"`, `"struct"`, `"event.listener"`) match the value’s dynamic class. Comparisons are case-insensitive.
Abstract categories (`"numeric"`, `"float"`, `"integer"`, `"handle"`, `"function_handle"`, `"gpuArray"`, `"listener"`) mirror MATLAB’s grouping rules.

Logical scalars and logical arrays satisfy `"logical"` and do not register as `"numeric"`. Internally auto-resident logical masks retain those host categories, while explicit gpuArray values expose the gpuArray wrapper instead.
Handle inheritance is respected: if a class derives from `handle`, `isa(obj, "handle")` returns `true` even when `class(obj)` reports a subclass name.
`isa` accepts either a string scalar or a character row vector as the class designator.
Resident inputs never need to be gathered. Only explicit user-visible residency matches `"gpuArray"`; internal automatic residency matches its underlying host class and categories.

faqs.question: Does `isa` treat gpuArray values as numeric?
faqs.answer: An explicit gpuArray exposes its wrapper identity and matches `"gpuArray"`, not the underlying numeric categories. RunMat's internal automatic residency remains transparent and matches the underlying host class and categories. Use `isUnderlyingType` to inspect an explicit gpuArray's element type.

faqs.question: How do I check for integer types?
faqs.answer: Use the `"integer"` category. It matches MATLAB’s native integer classes (`int8`, `uint16`, and so on). For example `isa(int32(5), "integer")` returns `true` while `isa(5, "integer")` returns `false`.

faqs.question: Does `isa` understand handle inheritance?
faqs.answer: Yes. If a class derives from `handle`, then the object passes the `"handle"` category check. The builtin walks parent classes registered with RunMat to mirror MATLAB semantics.

faqs.question: What kinds of strings can I pass as the type name?
faqs.answer: Provide either a string scalar (double quotes) or a character row vector (single quotes). Multi-row character arrays and string arrays with more than one element throw a descriptive error.

faqs.question: How do I detect function handles or anonymous functions?
faqs.answer: Both named function handles and closures pass `isa(value, "function_handle")`.

faqs.question: Will `isa` gather gpuArray inputs or launch kernels?
faqs.answer: No. The builtin is metadata-only and returns a host logical scalar without copying device buffers.

faqs.question: How are listeners treated?
faqs.answer: Event listeners pass both `isa(listener, "event.listener")` and the compatibility alias `isa(listener, "listener")`. They also satisfy the `"handle"` category.

faqs.question: Does `isa` differentiate between string and char arrays?
faqs.answer: Yes. String scalars pass `"string"` while character arrays pass `"char"`. They are not interchangeable.

faqs.question: Can I use `isa` to test meta-class values?
faqs.answer: Yes. Meta-class references created with `classref` return `true` for `"meta.class"`.

gpu_residency:
You usually do NOT need to call `gpuArray` yourself in RunMat (unlike MATLAB).

In RunMat, the fusion planner keeps residency on GPU in branches of fused expressions. As such, when you call `isa` on a gpuArray result, the planner preserves the device buffer and `isa` answers the query using metadata only.

To preserve backwards compatibility with MathWorks MATLAB, and for when you want to explicitly bootstrap GPU residency, you can call `gpuArray` explicitly to move data to the GPU if you want to be explicit about the residency.

Since MathWorks MATLAB does not have a fusion planner, and they kept their parallel execution toolbox separate from the core language, as their toolbox is a separate commercial product, MathWorks MATLAB users need to call `gpuArray` to move data to the GPU manually whereas RunMat users can rely on the fusion planner to keep data on the GPU automatically.
gpu_behavior: `isa` never launches GPU kernels. Explicit gpuArray inputs satisfy only the public wrapper identity `"gpuArray"`; internal automatic residency remains transparent and satisfies its underlying host class and categories. Because the builtin returns a host logical scalar from metadata, it does not participate in fusion and providers need no additional hooks.
